name: Draft animal power
desc: Oxen, horses and donkeys harnessed to pull, carry and turn machinery, the main non-human power source for millennia.

name: Horse mill
desc: A mill turned by animals walking in a circle, used to grind grain and later to drive pumps and early factories.

name: Treadwheel
desc: A large wheel turned by people or animals walking inside it, used to power cranes, pumps and mills.

name: Watermill
desc: A mill using a water wheel and gearing to grind grain or drive other machinery.

name: Ship mill
desc: A watermill mounted on a moored boat so its wheel sits in a river current.

name: Tide mill
desc: A watermill driven by tidal water impounded behind a dam and released on the ebb.

name: Panemone windmill
desc: A vertical-shaft windmill with sails rotating horizontally, the type built in medieval Persia.

name: Post mill
desc: The earliest European horizontal-axis windmill, whose whole body turns on a central post to face the wind.

name: Tower mill
desc: A windmill with a fixed masonry tower and a rotating cap carrying the sails, allowing larger mills.

name: Smock mill
desc: A tower-type windmill with a timber-framed, usually octagonal body and a rotating cap.

name: Trompe
desc: A water-powered air compressor with no moving parts, used to blow forges and later to drive mine machinery.

name: Windpump
desc: A multi-bladed self-regulating windmill for pumping water, which opened up dry grazing land.

name: Aeolipile
desc: Hero of Alexandria's spinning steam-jet sphere, the first recorded device turning steam into rotary motion.

name: Hydraulic ram
desc: A self-acting pump that uses the water-hammer effect of falling water to lift part of it higher.

name: Line shaft
desc: Overhead rotating shafts and belts that distributed power from one prime mover to many factory machines.

name: Hydraulic accumulator
desc: Armstrong's weighted ram storing water under pressure, which made hydraulic power networks practical.

name: Hydraulic power network
desc: City-wide networks of high-pressure water mains that powered lifts, cranes and presses before electricity.

name: Steam digester
desc: Denis Papin's pressure cooker, which pointed toward steam power and introduced the safety valve.

name: Safety valve
desc: A valve that opens automatically at a set pressure, invented for Papin's digester and essential to every boiler.

name: Beam engine
desc: A steam engine transmitting piston force through a rocking overhead beam, the form of Newcomen and Watt engines.

name: Centrifugal governor
desc: Spinning flyballs that throttle an engine to hold its speed constant, an early feedback controller.

name: Compound steam engine
desc: An engine expanding steam in successive cylinders, greatly improving fuel efficiency.

name: Flued boiler
desc: A cylindrical shell boiler with internal furnace flues (Cornish and Lancashire types) that made high-pressure steam practical.

name: Cornish engine
desc: Trevithick's high-pressure, expansive-working beam engine for mine pumping, far more economical than Watt's.

name: Fire-tube boiler
desc: A boiler in which hot gases pass through many tubes immersed in water, standard on locomotives.

name: Surface condenser
desc: A heat exchanger that condenses exhaust steam without mixing, returning pure water to the boiler.

name: Portable engine
desc: A wheeled steam engine hauled to farms and works to drive threshers and saws.

name: Economiser
desc: Green's heat exchanger using flue gas to preheat boiler feedwater, cutting fuel use.

name: Corliss steam engine
desc: A stationary engine with rotary valves and variable cutoff that set new standards of efficiency and speed regulation.

name: Superheater
desc: A device that heats steam above its boiling point, raising engine and turbine efficiency.

name: Feedwater heater
desc: Preheating boiler water with bled or exhaust steam to raise plant efficiency.

name: Injector
desc: Giffard's steam-driven jet pump for forcing feedwater into a boiler with no moving parts.

name: Rankine cycle
desc: The idealised vapour power cycle describing steam engines and turbine power plants.

name: Water-tube boiler
desc: A boiler with water inside tubes heated by external fire, allowing much higher pressures and outputs.

name: Brayton cycle
desc: The constant-pressure heat-addition cycle underlying gas turbines and jet engines.

name: Steam turbine
desc: Parsons's multi-stage turbine converting steam's energy directly into rotation, now the main generator drive.

name: De Laval nozzle
desc: A converging-diverging nozzle that accelerates gas to supersonic speed, used in impulse turbines and rockets.

name: Uniflow steam engine
desc: An engine in which steam flows one way through the cylinder, reducing heat losses.

name: Tesla turbine
desc: A bladeless turbine driven by fluid friction on closely spaced discs.

name: Pulverized coal-fired boiler
desc: A boiler burning finely ground coal blown into the furnace, the basis of large coal power stations.

name: Supercritical steam generator
desc: A boiler operating above water's critical point, raising the efficiency of thermal power plants.

name: Organic Rankine cycle
desc: A Rankine cycle using an organic working fluid to make power from low-temperature heat.

name: Water turbine
desc: An enclosed rotary machine extracting energy from flowing water, far more compact and efficient than a wheel.

name: Francis turbine
desc: An inward-flow reaction turbine for medium heads, the most widely used hydro turbine.

name: Pelton wheel
desc: An impulse turbine with split buckets struck by water jets, suited to very high heads.

name: Cross-flow turbine
desc: A drum-shaped turbine through which water passes twice, popular for small hydro schemes.

name: Kaplan turbine
desc: A propeller turbine with adjustable blades for low heads and large flows.

name: Turgo turbine
desc: An impulse turbine with jets striking the runner at an angle, for medium-high heads.

name: Bulb turbine
desc: A Kaplan-type turbine with the generator sealed in a bulb in the water flow, for very low heads.

name: Hydroelectricity
desc: Generating electricity from falling or flowing water, first at Cragside and soon in public plants.

name: Run-of-the-river hydroelectricity
desc: Hydro plants that use river flow with little or no storage reservoir.

name: Niagara Falls Adams power plant
desc: The first large-scale AC hydroelectric plant, sending Niagara power to Buffalo and proving long-distance AC.

name: Pumped-storage hydroelectricity
desc: Storing energy by pumping water uphill and releasing it through turbines, still the largest form of grid storage.

name: Hoover Dam
desc: A concrete arch-gravity dam on the Colorado River, a landmark of large multipurpose hydropower.

name: Three Gorges Dam
desc: The world's largest power station by installed capacity, on the Yangtze River.

name: Dynamo
desc: A commutated generator producing direct current, the first electrical machine able to deliver industrial power.

name: Gramme machine
desc: A ring-armature dynamo giving smooth, high DC output, the first commercially successful generator.

name: Power station
desc: A central plant generating electricity for many customers; Godalming and Pearl Street led the way in 1881-82.

name: Pearl Street Station
desc: Edison's first commercial central station in Manhattan, supplying DC light and power by underground mains.

name: Electric power transmission
desc: Moving bulk electricity over long distances by high-voltage lines from generators to load centres.

name: Electric power distribution
desc: The final stage of supply, carrying power from substations to consumers at lower voltages.

name: Overhead power line
desc: Bare conductors suspended from towers or poles, the cheapest way to carry bulk power.

name: Cogeneration
desc: Using a power plant's waste heat for heating or industry, raising total fuel efficiency.

name: Alternating current
desc: Current that reverses direction periodically, letting transformers step voltage up for efficient transmission.

name: Polyphase system
desc: Multiple AC phases offset in time, enabling rotating magnetic fields and Tesla's induction motor.

name: Electricity meter
desc: A device measuring electrical energy consumed, which made metered retail electricity possible.

name: Alternator
desc: A synchronous generator producing alternating current, the generator type in nearly all power plants.

name: Three-phase electric power
desc: The three-phase AC standard, demonstrated over 175 km from Lauffen to Frankfurt and now universal.

name: Electrical substation
desc: A facility that switches circuits and transforms voltage between transmission and distribution networks.

name: Mercury-arc valve
desc: A high-power rectifier using a mercury arc, which made the first HVDC links and electric traction supplies possible.

name: Electrostatic precipitator
desc: Cottrell's device removing fly ash and dust from flue gas with electric charge.

name: High-voltage direct current
desc: DC transmission for long distances and undersea cables with lower losses than AC, first commercial at Gotland.

name: Submarine power cable
desc: An insulated cable laid on the seabed to carry power to islands and offshore farms.

name: Combined-cycle power plant
desc: A plant feeding gas-turbine exhaust heat to a steam turbine, reaching over 60 percent efficiency.

name: Static VAR compensator
desc: Thyristor-switched reactors and capacitors that regulate grid voltage and reactive power.

name: Superconducting magnetic energy storage
desc: Storing energy in the magnetic field of a superconducting coil for near-instant release.

name: Demand response
desc: Shifting or curtailing consumer electricity use in response to grid conditions or prices.

name: Flexible AC transmission system
desc: Power-electronic controllers that increase the capacity and controllability of AC lines.

name: Smart meter
desc: A networked meter recording consumption at short intervals and communicating with the utility.

name: Smart grid
desc: A grid with digital sensing and two-way communication to balance variable supply and demand.

name: Microgrid
desc: A local grid with its own generation and storage that can run connected or islanded.

name: Charging station
desc: Public and home equipment for recharging electric vehicles, from early AC posts to modern DC fast chargers.

name: Vehicle-to-grid
desc: Using plugged-in electric vehicle batteries to feed power back and stabilise the grid.

name: Virtual power plant
desc: Software aggregating many small generators, batteries and loads to act as one power plant.

name: District heating
desc: Distributing heat from a central plant to many buildings through insulated pipes.

name: Heat pump
desc: A machine moving heat from a cold to a warm space, delivering several units of heat per unit of work.

name: Ground source heat pump
desc: A heat pump exchanging heat with the stable temperature of the ground for efficient heating and cooling.

name: Stirling engine
desc: A closed-cycle external-combustion engine using a regenerator, prized for quiet running and any heat source.

name: Four-stroke engine
desc: Otto's compression cycle of intake, compression, power and exhaust, the basis of most piston engines.

name: Two-stroke engine
desc: An engine completing its cycle in one revolution, simple and light for small machines.

name: Atkinson cycle
desc: An engine cycle with a longer expansion than compression stroke, now used in hybrid cars for efficiency.

name: Hot-bulb engine
desc: A low-compression engine igniting fuel in a heated bulb, widely used in tractors and boats.

name: Diesel engine
desc: Rudolf Diesel's compression-ignition engine, the most efficient common heat engine.

name: Wankel engine
desc: A rotary engine with a triangular rotor in an epitrochoid housing, compact but thirsty.

name: Longwall mining
desc: Extracting coal along a long face in a single slice, mechanised in the 20th century.

name: Coal gas
desc: Fuel gas from heating coal, which lit and heated cities through piped town-gas networks.

name: Gasholder
desc: A large telescoping tank storing town gas at constant pressure for distribution.

name: Davy lamp
desc: A miner's safety lamp whose wire gauze prevented ignition of firedamp, enabling deeper coal mining.

name: Bergius process
desc: Hydrogenating coal under high pressure to make synthetic liquid fuels.

name: Fischer–Tropsch process
desc: Catalytic conversion of carbon monoxide and hydrogen into liquid hydrocarbons, used for coal- and gas-to-liquids.

name: Flue-gas desulfurization
desc: Scrubbing sulfur dioxide from power-plant exhaust, first at Battersea, to curb acid rain.

name: Underground coal gasification
desc: Gasifying coal in place underground and drawing the syngas to the surface, first in the Soviet Union.

name: Continuous miner
desc: A machine that cuts and loads coal in one pass, replacing drilling and blasting.

name: Fluidized bed combustion
desc: Burning fuel in a bed of particles suspended by air, allowing low-grade fuels and in-bed sulfur capture.

name: Integrated gasification combined cycle
desc: A plant gasifying coal into syngas and burning it in a combined cycle, easing pollutant and CO2 capture.

name: Shale oil extraction
desc: Heating oil shale to release synthetic crude, an industry that predated drilled oil.

name: Kerosene
desc: A lamp fuel distilled first from coal and then petroleum, which created the early oil industry.

name: Drilling rig
desc: Structures and machinery for boring wells deep into the earth, evolving from cable tool to rotary drilling.

name: Pipeline transport
desc: Pipes carrying oil, gas and other fluids over long distances, first built in the Pennsylvania oil fields.

name: Offshore drilling
desc: Drilling for oil beneath the seabed, beginning from piers at Summerland, California.

name: Spindletop
desc: The Texas gusher drilled with rotary methods that launched the modern petroleum age.

name: Thermal cracking
desc: Breaking heavy oil molecules into lighter ones such as gasoline, first commercial in the Burton process.

name: Reflection seismology
desc: Mapping subsurface rock layers with reflected sound waves, the main tool of oil and gas exploration.

name: Blowout preventer
desc: A valve stack that seals a well to stop uncontrolled release of oil or gas.

name: Well logging
desc: Lowering instruments into a borehole to record rock properties, introduced by the Schlumberger brothers.

name: Directional drilling
desc: Steering a wellbore away from vertical, enabling horizontal wells that run along thin reservoirs.

name: Fluid catalytic cracking
desc: Cracking with a fluidized powdered catalyst, the main way refineries make high-octane gasoline.

name: Oil platform
desc: A large offshore structure for drilling and producing oil and gas out of sight of land.

name: Hydraulic fracturing
desc: Fracturing rock with high-pressure fluid to release oil and gas, transformative when combined with horizontal wells.

name: Catalytic reforming
desc: Converting low-octane naphtha into high-octane reformate over a platinum catalyst, yielding hydrogen too.

name: Enhanced oil recovery
desc: Injecting steam, gas or chemicals to recover oil left behind by primary production.

name: Oil sands extraction
desc: Mining or steaming bitumen out of sand deposits and upgrading it to synthetic crude.

name: FPSO
desc: A floating vessel that produces, stores and offloads oil, opening deep-water fields.

name: Steam-assisted gravity drainage
desc: Paired horizontal wells inject steam and drain heated bitumen from deep oil sands.

name: Shale gas
desc: Natural gas from shale made economic by slickwater fracking of horizontal wells, reshaping energy markets.

name: Tight oil
desc: Light crude produced from low-permeability shale by fracked horizontal wells, as in the Bakken and Permian.

name: Natural gas
desc: Methane-rich gas from underground, burned in Han China to boil brine and piped commercially from the 1820s.

name: Liquefied petroleum gas
desc: Propane and butane stored as liquid under modest pressure, a portable fuel for cooking and heating.

name: Liquefied natural gas
desc: Natural gas cooled to a liquid for shipping and storage at 1/600 of its volume.

name: Steam reforming
desc: Making hydrogen by reacting methane with steam over a catalyst, the main source of industrial hydrogen.

name: Amine gas treating
desc: Absorbing CO2 and hydrogen sulfide from gas streams with amine solutions, the basis of carbon capture.

name: Compressed natural gas
desc: Natural gas stored at high pressure as a vehicle fuel.

name: LNG carrier
desc: A tanker with insulated cryogenic tanks that turned natural gas into a global seaborne commodity.

name: Coalbed methane
desc: Natural gas recovered from coal seams, developed commercially in the US from the 1980s.

name: Gas to liquids
desc: Converting natural gas into diesel and other liquid fuels via Fischer–Tropsch synthesis.

name: Heavy water production
desc: Deuterium oxide concentrated by electrolysis at Vemork, used as a neutron moderator in reactors.

name: Nuclear reprocessing
desc: Chemically separating plutonium and uranium from spent fuel, via the PUREX process from 1949.

name: Uranium enrichment
desc: Raising the fraction of fissile U-235 in uranium, needed for most reactor fuel.

name: Gaseous diffusion
desc: Separating uranium isotopes by passing UF6 through porous barriers, as at Oak Ridge K-25.

name: Breeder reactor
desc: A reactor producing more fissile fuel than it consumes; EBR-I also made the first nuclear electricity.

name: Nuclear power plant
desc: A thermal power station heated by fission, first grid-connected at Obninsk in 1954.

name: Pressurized water reactor
desc: A light-water reactor whose pressurised coolant heats a separate steam loop, the dominant reactor type.

name: Magnox reactor
desc: A British gas-cooled, graphite-moderated reactor on natural uranium; Calder Hall was the first.

name: Boiling water reactor
desc: A light-water reactor that boils its coolant directly to drive the turbine.

name: Gas centrifuge
desc: Spinning uranium hexafluoride to separate isotopes, far more energy-efficient than gaseous diffusion.

name: Sodium-cooled fast reactor
desc: A fast-neutron reactor cooled by liquid sodium, the main breeder design.

name: Radioisotope thermoelectric generator
desc: A generator turning decay heat into electricity, powering spacecraft and remote beacons for decades.

name: CANDU reactor
desc: A Canadian heavy-water reactor that runs on natural uranium and refuels on line.

name: MOX fuel
desc: Reactor fuel blending plutonium and uranium oxides, recycling separated plutonium.

name: Molten-salt reactor
desc: A reactor with fuel dissolved in molten fluoride salt, demonstrated by Oak Ridge's MSRE.

name: Pebble-bed reactor
desc: A helium-cooled reactor fuelled by graphite pebbles, high-temperature and passively safe.

name: Lead-cooled fast reactor
desc: A fast reactor cooled by molten lead or lead-bismuth eutectic; few have been built, the best-known lead-cooled reactors being those of Soviet submarine K-27 and the Alfa class, which were beryllium-moderated intermediate-energy designs rather than fast reactors.

name: RBMK
desc: A Soviet graphite-moderated, water-cooled channel reactor, the type that failed at Chernobyl.

name: Advanced gas-cooled reactor
desc: The second-generation British reactor with CO2 coolant and enriched oxide fuel.

name: Dry cask storage
desc: Storing cooled spent fuel in sealed steel and concrete casks on site.

name: Generation III reactor
desc: Evolved light-water designs with improved fuel, passive safety and longer life.

name: Deep geological repository
desc: Mined storage deep in stable rock for long-lived radioactive waste.

name: Small modular reactor
desc: A factory-built reactor of under about 300 MW, first operating afloat in Russia in 2020.

name: Z-pinch
desc: Confining plasma by the magnetic field of a strong axial current, one of the first fusion concepts.

name: Magnetic confinement fusion
desc: Holding hot fusion plasma in magnetic fields, the main path pursued toward fusion power.

name: Stellarator
desc: Spitzer's fusion device confining plasma with externally twisted magnetic coils.

name: Tokamak
desc: A Soviet toroidal fusion device with a plasma current, the leading magnetic confinement design.

name: Fusor
desc: Farnsworth's inertial electrostatic confinement device, a simple neutron source that achieves fusion.

name: Inertial confinement fusion
desc: Compressing fuel pellets with lasers or particle beams until they fuse before flying apart.

name: Joint European Torus
desc: The largest tokamak of its era, which set fusion energy records with deuterium-tritium fuel.

name: Spherical tokamak
desc: A compact, low-aspect-ratio tokamak, demonstrated by START at Culham.

name: Wendelstein 7-X
desc: A computer-optimised superconducting stellarator in Germany testing steady-state confinement.

name: NIF fusion ignition
desc: In December 2022 NIF's laser-driven implosion released more fusion energy than the laser energy delivered.

name: Wind turbine
desc: A wind-driven electricity generator; Friedlander's 1883 Vienna machine was first, then Blyth and Brush in 1887.

name: Vertical-axis wind turbine
desc: Wind turbines whose rotor shaft is vertical, accepting wind from any direction.

name: Savonius wind turbine
desc: A simple drag-type vertical-axis turbine made of curved scoops.

name: Darrieus wind turbine
desc: A lift-type vertical-axis wind turbine with curved blades.

name: Smith–Putnam wind turbine
desc: The first megawatt-scale wind turbine, synchronised to a utility grid in Vermont.

name: Wind farm
desc: Arrays of utility-scale turbines feeding the grid, begun in California's wind rush.

name: Offshore wind power
desc: Wind farms at sea, first at Vindeby in Denmark, using stronger and steadier winds.

name: Floating offshore wind
desc: Turbines on moored floating platforms for waters too deep for fixed foundations.

name: Solar cooker
desc: A glazed hot box or reflector concentrating sunlight to cook food, first built by de Saussure.

name: Photovoltaic effect
desc: Becquerel's discovery that light falling on certain materials generates a voltage.

name: Solar water heating
desc: Collectors that heat water with sunlight, sold commercially from the 1890s.

name: Parabolic trough
desc: Curved mirrors focusing sunlight on a pipe; Shuman's 1912 Egyptian plant pumped irrigation water.

name: Concentrated solar power
desc: Generating electricity by concentrating sunlight to drive a heat engine, with thermal storage for night.

name: Solar furnace
desc: A field of mirrors concentrating sunlight to over 3000 C, as at Odeillo in France.

name: Solar tracker
desc: A mount that turns panels or mirrors to follow the sun, raising energy yield.

name: Thin-film solar cell
desc: Cells made of micron-thin layers such as amorphous silicon, using far less material.

name: CIGS solar cell
wiki: Copper indium gallium selenide solar cell
desc: A thin-film cell using copper indium gallium selenide, flexible and efficient.

name: Concentrator photovoltaics
desc: Using lenses or mirrors to focus sunlight onto small high-efficiency cells.

name: Solar inverter
desc: Converts DC from solar panels to grid AC and tracks the panels' maximum power point.

name: Solar power tower
desc: Heliostats focusing sunlight on a central receiver tower, often storing heat in molten salt.

name: Cadmium telluride photovoltaics
desc: The cheapest thin-film technology, mass-produced from the 2000s.

name: Solar updraft tower
desc: A large greenhouse and chimney driving air through turbines, demonstrated at Manzanares in Spain.

name: Photovoltaic power station
desc: Utility-scale solar farms feeding the grid, now the fastest-growing source of electricity.

name: Multi-junction solar cell
desc: Stacked cells of different band gaps reaching the highest efficiencies, used on spacecraft.

name: Thermal energy storage
desc: Storing heat or cold, for example in molten salt at solar plants, for later use.

name: Organic solar cell
desc: Cells built from carbon-based semiconductors, potentially cheap and flexible.

name: Heterojunction solar cell
desc: Crystalline silicon wafers coated with amorphous silicon layers for high efficiency.

name: Dye-sensitized solar cell
desc: The Graetzel cell, using a dye on titanium dioxide to mimic photosynthesis.

name: Building-integrated photovoltaics
desc: Solar cells built into roofs, facades and glazing as part of the building envelope.

name: Agrivoltaics
desc: Sharing land between solar panels and crops or grazing.

name: Quantum dot solar cell
desc: Cells using semiconductor nanocrystals whose band gap is tuned by size.

name: Floating solar
desc: Solar arrays mounted on pontoons on reservoirs and lakes.

name: Perovskite solar cell
desc: Cells using perovskite-structured absorbers whose efficiency rose faster than any prior PV material.

name: Geothermal heating
desc: Using hot springs and ground heat directly to warm buildings, as at Chaudes-Aigues from the 14th century.

name: Geothermal power
desc: Generating electricity from underground steam or hot water, first at Larderello, Italy.

name: Binary cycle power
desc: Using moderate-temperature geothermal water to boil a secondary fluid that drives the turbine.

name: Enhanced geothermal system
desc: Creating heat reservoirs in hot dry rock by hydraulic stimulation, trialled at Fenton Hill.

name: Tidal power
desc: Electricity from tidal range or currents; the Rance barrage in France opened in 1966.

name: Tidal stream generator
desc: Underwater rotors driven by tidal currents, like wind turbines in water.

name: Wave power
desc: Capturing the energy of ocean waves; early devices date to c. 1910 and Masuda's 1940s navigation-light buoys.

name: Ocean thermal energy conversion
desc: Running a heat engine on the temperature difference between warm surface and cold deep seawater.

name: Osmotic power
desc: Generating power from the salinity difference between fresh and seawater, prototyped in Norway.

name: Biogas
desc: Methane-rich gas from anaerobic digestion of organic waste, used for cooking, heat and power.

name: Anaerobic digester
desc: Sealed tanks where microbes break down sewage or manure into biogas, as at Exeter in 1895.

name: Waste-to-energy
desc: Burning municipal waste to produce steam and electricity, from Victorian refuse destructors onward.

name: Ethanol fuel
desc: Alcohol from crops burned as motor fuel, mass-adopted in Brazil from 1975.

name: Wood gas generator
desc: A gasifier turning wood or charcoal into fuel gas to run engines, common in wartime fuel shortages.

name: Biodiesel
desc: Diesel fuel made by transesterifying vegetable oils or animal fats.

name: Sustainable aviation fuel
desc: Jet fuel from biomass, waste oils or synthesis, cutting lifecycle aviation emissions.

name: Cellulosic ethanol
desc: Ethanol made from inedible plant fibre by enzymatic or thermochemical breakdown.

name: Thermoelectric effect
desc: Seebeck's discovery that a temperature difference across joined metals produces a voltage.

name: Daniell cell
desc: A two-electrolyte copper-zinc cell giving steady current, which powered early telegraphs.

name: Lead–acid battery
desc: Planté's rechargeable battery, still standard for car starting and backup power.

name: Leclanché cell
desc: A zinc and manganese dioxide cell with ammonium chloride electrolyte, ancestor of the dry cell.

name: Zinc–carbon battery
desc: Gassner's sealed dry cell, the first mass-market portable battery.

name: Nickel–cadmium battery
desc: Jungner's rugged rechargeable alkaline battery, later sealed for portable devices.

name: Nickel–iron battery
desc: Edison's very durable alkaline storage battery for vehicles and railways.

name: Zinc–air battery
desc: A battery oxidising zinc with oxygen from the air, very energy-dense, used in hearing aids.

name: Mercury battery
desc: Ruben's zinc-mercuric oxide cell with steady voltage, later banned for its mercury.

name: Alkaline battery
desc: Urry's zinc-manganese dioxide cell with alkaline electrolyte, longer-lasting than zinc-carbon.

name: Silver oxide battery
desc: A high-energy primary button cell for watches and calculators.

name: Lithium primary battery
desc: Non-rechargeable cells with lithium anodes, offering high energy density and long shelf life.

name: Nickel–hydrogen battery
desc: A long-lived rechargeable battery with a pressurised hydrogen electrode, used on satellites and Hubble.

name: Lithium cobalt oxide cathode
desc: Goodenough's layered intercalation cathode that made the lithium-ion battery practical.

name: Nickel–metal hydride battery
desc: A rechargeable battery with a hydrogen-absorbing alloy anode, used in early hybrid cars.

name: Solid-state battery
desc: A battery with a solid electrolyte, from thin-film LiPON cells toward safer, denser EV batteries.

name: Lithium iron phosphate battery
desc: A cobalt-free lithium-ion chemistry that is safer and longer-lived, now common in EVs and storage.

name: Lithium manganese oxide battery
desc: A lithium-ion chemistry with a spinel manganese cathode, cheap and thermally stable.

name: Lithium polymer battery
desc: A lithium-ion battery with a polymer or gel electrolyte in a flexible pouch.

name: NCA cathode
desc: Nickel-cobalt-aluminium cathodes with very high energy density, used in Tesla cars.

name: NMC cathode
desc: Nickel-manganese-cobalt layered cathodes giving the high energy density of most EV batteries.

name: Lithium-titanate battery
desc: A lithium-ion battery with a titanate anode allowing very fast charging and long cycle life.

name: Lithium–sulfur battery
desc: A light, high-energy battery with a sulfur cathode, used in high-altitude drones.

name: Sodium-ion battery
desc: A lithium-ion analogue using abundant sodium, reaching mass-produced cars in 2023.

name: Sodium–sulfur battery
desc: A molten-salt battery with a ceramic electrolyte, used for grid storage.

name: Flow battery
desc: A rechargeable battery storing energy in liquid electrolytes in external tanks, scalable for the grid.

name: Zinc–bromine battery
desc: A hybrid flow battery plating zinc from a bromide electrolyte, for stationary storage.

name: Vanadium redox battery
desc: A flow battery using vanadium in both electrolytes, avoiding cross-contamination.

name: Supercapacitor
desc: A double-layer capacitor storing far more charge than ordinary capacitors, for fast bursts of power.

name: Flywheel energy storage
desc: Storing energy in a spinning rotor, first in the Swiss gyrobus and now for grid frequency control.

name: Compressed-air energy storage
desc: Storing energy as compressed air in caverns, first at Huntorf in Germany.

name: Liquid air energy storage
desc: Storing energy by liquefying air and later expanding it through a turbine.

name: Battery energy storage system
desc: Grid-connected battery banks for balancing and backup, scaled up with lithium-ion from the 2010s.

name: Hornsdale Power Reserve
desc: A 100 MW lithium-ion grid battery in South Australia that showed batteries could stabilise a grid.

name: Electrolysis of water
desc: Splitting water into hydrogen and oxygen with electric current, now central to green hydrogen.

name: Fuel cell
desc: Grove's gas battery converting hydrogen and oxygen directly into electricity.

name: Solid oxide fuel cell
desc: A high-temperature fuel cell with a ceramic electrolyte that can run on hydrocarbons.

name: Alkaline fuel cell
desc: Bacon's practical hydrogen-oxygen cell, which powered the Apollo spacecraft.

name: Molten carbonate fuel cell
desc: A high-temperature fuel cell with a molten carbonate electrolyte, for stationary power.

name: Hydrogen storage
desc: Compressed, liquefied or material-based methods of storing hydrogen fuel.

name: Proton-exchange membrane fuel cell
desc: A low-temperature fuel cell with a polymer membrane, used on Gemini and in fuel-cell cars.

name: PEM electrolysis
desc: Splitting water across a solid polymer membrane, suited to variable renewable power.

name: Hydrogen economy
desc: A proposed energy system using hydrogen as the main carrier for transport, industry and storage.

name: Phosphoric acid fuel cell
desc: The first commercially sold fuel cell type, used for building power and heat.

name: Solid oxide electrolyzer cell
desc: A fuel cell run in reverse at high temperature to split steam efficiently.

name: Direct methanol fuel cell
desc: A PEM fuel cell oxidising liquid methanol directly, for portable power.

name: Power-to-gas
desc: Converting surplus electricity into hydrogen or synthetic methane for storage in gas networks.

name: Carbon capture and storage
desc: Capturing CO2 from industry or power plants and storing it underground.

name: Bioenergy with carbon capture
